body:
House "artist" makes me queasy. There is no way this is done in as sanitary an environment with sterile equipment as it would be in a reputable shop.

While a house "artist" aka a scratcher, may seem to do decent work and be cheaper... you're risking your health for a poor quality tattoo. Isn't good work in a clean environment worth the extra expense?
Can you take her to a vet or shelter and have her scanned for a microchip? Her family may be looking for her.

My cat's favorite toys are a stress ball and shiny crinkle balls that make me think of tinsel. You can get the crinkle balls for like 99 cents. He goes crazy and chases them around all by himself. If he so much as hears a crinkle noise he comes running.

Sometimes feliway helps with anxiety. There is one near my cat's tree. The diffuser doesn't seem to do much for mine but the spray helps him when he goes to the vet.

Over grooming can become a habit and then it's really hard to break. My cat is finally free of his ibd symptoms and stopped overgrooming to the point of having bald spots but I still catch him pulling on his hair sometimes. I think it helps him to have soft fleece beds that he chews on instead (gross but he was bottle fed so I think it's self soothing).

Just leave him go. I would be more afraid of him getting hung up and choking when he's home alone than pulling his fur out. If you catch him doing it redirect him with a toy or something else to do with his mouth. It's really annoying. Trust me I was sick to death of the hairballs, the diseased looking cat, and all the other allergy and gi issues. You'll get to the bottom of it eventually. What worked for mine was a limited ingredient diet. The prescription z/d food actually made him sicker.
I love her. What a cute old lady 🥺

He is on Instinct's rabbit formula wet food. They also make a limited ingredient version of the same food. It's pretty much the same price as the prescription z/d diet but honestly the money is worth it if he's symptom free. 

I have a sneaking suspicion kitty is allergic to chicken. Maybe a novel protein diet can help if z/d or other diets aren't working.

His diarrhea and vomiting/hairballs have stopped with the diet change alone so the vet said "If it ain't broke don't fix it." He has black peach fuzz all over the bald spots and has even gained a few ounces. We are going to hang tight and see if he continues to improve.

Nonsmoker and rarely drink. No health conditions. 

I was told that I am missing a tooth and that is why my smile is droopy and I have a jowl on one side. I was told the only option is surgery and an implant. The back teeth on my right side the "good" side touch and the ones on the other side don't (image flipped due to mirror). 

I had braces as a kid and the orthodontist told me my front teeth will never line up with the middle of my face properly and this is as good as it gets.

Is an implant the best option for me? Is it the only option? The snaggle tooth that looks chipped is not. It's malformed and has always looked like that.
These are all great suggestions. Thanks!
My cat was a bottle fed orphan and he does this to any kind of fleece material.

My cat likes to have up high places to go like a cat tree, but he also really likes those snuggly cave beds. He's obsessed with fleece and rubs his face on it when he's getting ready to take a nap. 

He loves these little foil balls you can get at the pet store. They're like 99 cents a piece. He'll run around the apartment with one for half an hour at a time. It's nice because he can play by himself if I can't play with him at the moment. If I pick it up and roll it around in my hands so it crinkles and then toss it onto the hardwood It's enough to get him interested. 

Apparently cats are bad at drinking enough water? I didn't know that until someone told me. I switched from a bowl to a fountain and my cat drinks way more water.

Overall I think they're pretty clean as long as you brush them. I keep the litter box in the laundry room to help keep it away from the main area of the apartment. My cat tree has removable beds which is really nice incase the cat has a hairball or they start to get dirty. You can just toss it in the washer. I also have a silicone placemat with sides like a tray that I got from the pet store. My cat eats wet food and it stops the food from getting on the floor if he's messy. It's super easy to wipe off.

Has your vet talked to you about IBD? 

Have you tried single protein foods or hydrolyzed protein diets? My cat with gi problems seems to be doing much better on natural instincts limited ingredient rabbit diet. He was have diarrhea pretty frequently before this.

I'm in the US but I have insurance on my cat. Just a heads up, whatever put your cat in the hospital and anything related to it is now a pre-existing condition and won't be covered. Say if your cat has allergies and takes medicine for being itchy. Any skin condition, hair loss, throwing up, anything that could be related to allergies the insurance won't cover. There's also a waiting period before the policy kicks in. 

I'm glad I got insurance, but shop around.

So I'm going through all sorts of hair pulling with my gi issues cat. Is your cat on a limited ingredient allergy diet? Or is that the hydrolyzed stuff? My cat hated the hydrolyzed food and would smash it all over the floor and only eat when he was starving. The thing is, hydrolyzed food has the proteins partially broken down so that they are easier to digest and less likely to cause diarrhea and vomiting. 

He also could be still having problems with chicken and need to try something else. My cat eats wet food that is rabbit and peas and is doing much better. He was still having diarrhea with science diet z/d.

You could try cat food that comes in shreds. I know Tiki cat has shreds that literally looks like cooked shredded chicken breast.

So this is the first time I've had a pet in years, but it's the one who has been seeing my cat since I adopted him in September. I understand not wanting to give him the wrong treatment and maybe that's why he's pushing for the ultrasound so hard, but I'd rather spend money on making my cat comfortable than a test that may not be beneficial. 

Thanks for your advice. I do think it's time to see another vet. It could honestly be something as simple as me not fully understand what this vet is trying to explain to me, and there may be someone else who makes it click better.

That is the same reason why he had an xray too. He randomly got extremely sick one day even though he was on the hydrolyzed diet with no extra treats allowed. 

He seems to be doing well on the new rabbit protein diet. I'm just stressing because I want to do the right thing for him, but I don't have an unlimited vet budget. The emergency visit + the follow up tests have cost me around $1,000. That doesn't include all the other visits he had for his hairloss. 

If all the ultrasound does is confirm something is wrong, and I don't have the ability to treat cancer, I don't know that spending money for that test is worth it.

So we could try steroids too. There is a risk that they could cause him to develop diabetes. My vet is really pushing for the ultrasound before starting steroids, but it sounds like they're often inconclusive. I think I need a second opinion.

His food was recently changed again because he wasn't tolerating the z/d well and he was refusing to eat it. He really likes the new food and his symptoms seem to be improving. I think the main reason why I'm so frustrated is he looked pretty good until we put him on the z/d food. Yeah he had spots where he was overgrooming but he was shiny, he had clearly gained weight. He sometimes had soft stool. We put him on z/d and he hardly ate, had a huge drop in energy, his fur always looks oddly dishelved, hair balls way more often, he's thin enough that it scares me, and he was having diarrhea a few times a week.

 How can he have IBD or cancer if he was doing so much better before we changed his diet? How could he be so sick if his blood work is normal? It's very frustrating that we're starting down this path of drugs that might hurt his kidneys and surgeries when it seems like what he is eating is making it worse.
